spec_match.rationale: Runs six genuine handshakes covering empty offer, single, server-preference ordering, unknown-only failure, and the duplicate SyntaxError — the constructor's negotiation contract as the WebSockets Standard states it.

interactive.rationale: Run all six opens real connections and fills a live table with per-case expected-vs-observed verdicts plus an aria-live summary; verified 6/6 matched after clicking.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises several/unknown/none offers with server-preference selection and the page demonstrates each in its own row.

edge_cases.rationale: Failure branches are the point of the page: failed handshake for unknown-only offers, construction-time duplicate error, and the empty-offer non-error are all exercised live.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5080055102439424 and the constructor section of the WebSockets Standard.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite asserts the same negotiation contracts this page shows (sequence negotiates server preference, empty protocol opens cleanly, duplicates throw); /conformance/ ran 5 pass / 1 fail on Chromium 141, the fail being the dictionary-read assertion that needs Chrome 154.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): clicked Run all six, all six rows matched expectations including the handshake failure and duplicate SyntaxError, console showed only the page's own logs, no failed same-origin requests; desktop 1280 and mobile 360 screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and emits a negotiation-run assert with matched/total on each run.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, button background and color set together, no static-card pattern.

accessibility.rationale: Captioned table with scoped th cells, aria-live output for the run summary, single labelled button with 44px min-height.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read); the five-column table wraps its headers rather than clipping.

openQuestions.title: Offer the options-bag form in at least one negotiation case when supported
openQuestions.detail: Every case constructs with the positional form, so on Chrome 154 the page never actually exercises the shipped { protocols } dictionary it sits under. Negotiation semantics are identical by design, but adding one case (or a toggle) that constructs via the options bag when the getter probe says it is supported would let the page prove that equivalence within its own subject matter instead of delegating it entirely to the both-forms concept.

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/add-options-bag-to-websocket-constructor/negotiation/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp). Clicked Run all six via CDP; all six live handshakes matched the documented rules (6/6), including the server-preference row negotiating echo over chat, the unknown-only handshake failure, and the duplicate-subprotocol construction error. Desktop 1280 and mobile 360 DPR3 screenshots read, no overflow, console/network clean apart from the sandbox font-CDN cert artifact; the injected browser-support panel and /conformance/ route both ran the suite at 5 pass / 1 fail, the fail being the Chrome-154-only dictionary assertion. This concept works fully even on this pre-154 browser since it exercises negotiation, not the new dictionary shape.
